title: [NEXT-1121] Unexpected object mutation in `generateMetadata`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: linear: next
labels.description: Confirmed issue that is tracked by the Next.js team.

body: ### Verify canary release - [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release ### Provide environment information ```bash Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.4.0: Mon Mar 6 20:59:28 PST 2023; root:xnu-8796.101.5~3/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 Binaries: Node: 18.12.1 npm: 8.19.2 Yarn: 1.22.19 pnpm: 8.4.0 Relevant packages: next: 13.4.2-canary.3 eslint-config-next: 13.4.1 react: 18.2.0 react-dom: 18.2.0 typescript: 5.0.4 ``` ### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure) App directory (appDir: true), Metadata (metadata, generateMetadata, next/head, head.js) ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/runjuu/url-object-are-not-supported ### To Reproduce ``` npm run dev ``` Open http://localhost:3000/ , and then check Terminal's logs ### Describe the Bug The issue was caused by the [resolveImages](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/8d228780e72706ef4bd5b6327ede2c0340181353/packages/next/src/lib/metadata/resolvers/resolve-opengraph.ts#L49-L51) method, where the input array is altered by substituting it with a `URL` class. This modification results in a React error, stating that URL objects cannot be passed to Client Components from Server Components. This problem is likely to occur when using shared configurations or relying on cached fetch results. #### Complete Error Message: ``` Warning: Only plain objects can be passed to Client Components from Server Components. URL objects are not supported. {url: URL} ^^^ ``` ### Expected Behavior Do not mutate the passed object. ### Which browser are you using? (if relevant) _No response_ ### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant) _No response_ [NEXT-1121](https://linear.app/vercel/issue/NEXT-1121/unexpected-object-mutation-in-generatemetadata)
